en: If one has oneself violated the commitments (*samaya*), one should likewise receive such an initiation exactly as the procedure for the entry of the master prescribes for its reception; however, this is only if the true guru resides in a very distant place, in a region inaccessible due to obstacles such as difficult paths, and not otherwise.

However, by always undertaking [the practice] through the yoga of one’s chosen deity, whose nature is the single flavor of wisdom and means, within the mentally constructed mandala, one should receive from the Lord of the Mandala the water initiation and so forth, up to the secret, wisdom, and fourth initiations, as well as up to the pledges of the breaths; such is the procedure for one's own initiation.

If one’s own samaya is impaired, one should receive this very empowerment in the same manner as it was prescribed for the master’s entry into the ritual dance (*maṇḍala*). However, this applies only in cases where one resides in a location that cannot be reached due to circumstances such as being extremely distant from a sublime guru or the presence of difficult travel routes; it does not apply otherwise.

Regarding constant practice of the *iṣṭadevatā*: having meditated with the mind on the natural maṇḍala through the yoga of one’s chosen deity, in which wisdom and method are of one taste, one should receive from the Lord of the Maṇḍala the water initiation and so forth, up to the secret, the wisdom-knowledge (*prajñājñāna*), and the fourth [initiation], culminating in the final exhalation (*ucchvāsa*).
This is the ritual for the self-initiation.
